6. Overdraft basics
An arranged overdraft is a credit facility attached to a current account. It allows the balance to go below zero up to an approved limit. Arranged overdrafts are subject to credit assessment and are not guaranteed. Details are in [Loans, Overdrafts & Credit Assessment](05_loans_overdrafts_and_credit_assessment.md).
An unarranged overdraft occurs when the account goes below zero without approval or exceeds an arranged limit. Aurora Bank may refuse payments that would create or increase an unarranged overdraft. Fees and interest may apply as described in [Fees, Interest & Foreign Exchange](06_fees_interest_and_exchange_rates.md).
Youth accounts, Basic Payment Accounts, savings accounts, and Fixed Term Deposits do not offer arranged overdrafts.

9. Arranged overdrafts
An arranged overdraft is intended as a short-term borrowing facility. It should not be used for long-term borrowing or regular living costs. Aurora Bank may review, reduce, suspend, or cancel an overdraft after notice or immediately where required for risk, fraud, legal, or account-conduct reasons.
Important overdraft rules:
- Interest is charged only on the used arranged overdraft balance.
- The overdraft is repayable on demand.
- Exceeding the limit may lead to declined payments and fees.
- An overdraft limit is not a promise that every payment will be honored.
- Savings accounts and youth accounts do not have overdrafts.

Arranged overdraft interest is calculated daily on the used arranged overdraft balance and charged monthly. The illustrative arranged overdraft rate is 13.90% annual nominal variable.

However, payments that exceed the available balance may be rejected and failed-payment fees may apply where permitted. 8. Direct debits, standing orders, and recurring payments
Direct debits are authorized by the customer to allow a payee to collect variable or fixed amounts. Standing orders are instructions created by the customer to pay a fixed amount on a schedule. Recurring card payments are card-authorized merchant arrangements and are not the same as direct debits.
Cancellation rules differ:
- A standing order can normally be cancelled in online banking before the processing cutoff.
- A direct debit can be cancelled with Aurora Bank, but the customer should also cancel the agreement with the merchant.
- A recurring card payment should be cancelled with the merchant. Aurora Bank can block future merchant attempts in some cases, but this may not cancel the underlying contract.
Payment execution and cancellation timings are described in [Payments, Transfers & Cutoff Times](03_payments_transfers_and_cutoff_times.md).

8. Direct debits
A direct debit allows an organization to collect money from the customer’s account under a mandate. The customer should receive advance notice from the payee unless the scheme rules allow otherwise.
Aurora Bank can cancel a direct debit mandate on the account, but this does not cancel the underlying contract with the merchant. The merchant may still claim the amount by another method or treat the customer as overdue.
Where a direct debit is unauthorized or collected incorrectly, the customer may have refund rights under applicable payment-scheme and legal rules. Dispute processes are explained in [Disputes, Chargebacks & Fraud Claims](07_disputes_chargebacks_and_fraud_claims.md).

11. Cancelling, recalling, or amending a payment
Cancellation rights depend on payment type.
| Payment type | Can the customer cancel? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Future-dated SEPA payment | Usually yes before cutoff on the business day before execution. | Online cancellation may be available. |
| Standing order | Usually yes before the cutoff for the next due date. | Cancelling does not cancel contracts with merchants. |
| Direct debit | Usually yes before cutoff on the business day before collection. | Customer should also notify the payee. |
| SEPA instant transfer | Usually no once authorized. | Recall can be attempted but is not guaranteed. |
| Standard SEPA transfer | Recall can be requested after execution. | Recipient bank and recipient consent may be required. |
| International wire | Amendment or recall can be requested. | Fees apply and recovery is not guaranteed. |
| Card purchase | Customer should first contact merchant unless fraud is suspected. | Chargeback may be possible under card scheme rules. |
Aurora Bank cannot guarantee recovery of funds sent to the wrong recipient if the payment was authorized by the customer. The bank may try to contact the receiving bank, but the recipient may need to consent to return funds unless legal rules allow reversal.

Cutoff times are shown in Central European Time unless otherwise stated. They can change during public holidays, system maintenance, or payment-scheme disruption.

|---|---:|---|

6. Time limits
Customers should raise disputes promptly. Card-scheme time limits can be short and may run from transaction date, expected delivery date, cancellation date, or merchant promise date.
Indicative timeframes:
| Claim type | Customer should report by | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Unauthorized card transaction | Immediately, and no later than 13 months where legal rules permit | Faster reporting can reduce loss. |
| Goods or services not received | After expected delivery date, usually within 120 days of expected receipt | Scheme rules vary. |
| Refund not processed | After merchant’s refund timeframe, usually within 120 days of refund promise | Evidence needed. |
| ATM cash not dispensed | Within 30 days if possible | ATM balancing may be time-sensitive. |
| Incorrect direct debit | As soon as noticed | Scheme and legal refund rights may apply. |
| Payment sent to wrong account | Immediately | Recovery becomes harder once funds move. |
The exact deadline depends on scheme and legal rules. Aurora Bank may be unable to pursue a claim filed too late.

10. Open banking
Open banking allows a customer to give a regulated third-party provider access to account information or payment initiation services. Aurora Bank will provide access only after the customer gives permission through the required secure process.
Important open banking points:
- Aurora Bank will never ask the customer to share online banking passwords with a third-party provider.
- The customer can withdraw open banking consent through Aurora online banking or the third-party provider.
- Revoking access does not delete data already received by the third-party provider.
- The third-party provider is responsible for its own use of data after it receives it.
- Payment initiation through open banking may still require strong customer authentication.
Customers should use only regulated providers and should check the provider name carefully before approving access.

Security, Online Banking & Customer Responsibilities
1. Security principles
Aurora Bank uses layered security controls to protect accounts. These controls may include encryption, device binding, login monitoring, fraud scoring, strong customer authentication, payment warnings, transaction limits, account locks, and manual review.
Security controls may occasionally delay payments, block card use, restrict online access, or require additional verification. Aurora Bank will not compensate for inconvenience where a control was applied reasonably for safety or legal compliance.

Security, Online Banking & Customer Responsibilities
7. New payee and payment verification
When setting up a new payee, customers should verify the account number through a trusted channel. For invoices, the customer should confirm changes to bank details using a known phone number, not contact details on the changed invoice.
Aurora Bank may delay, hold, or reject first payments to new payees, high-risk merchants, crypto-asset platforms, or countries with elevated risk.

10. Secure messages and document upload
Customers should send sensitive information only through approved secure channels. Documents uploaded to online banking should be clear, complete, and unaltered. Aurora Bank may reject documents that are cropped, blurry, password-protected, edited, or inconsistent.
Customers should not send identity documents, card numbers, passwords, or one-time passcodes through ordinary email unless specifically instructed through a secure process.

Security, Online Banking & Customer Responsibilities
2. Strong customer authentication
Strong customer authentication uses at least two independent elements from the following categories:
- something the customer knows, such as password or PIN;
- something the customer has, such as registered device or hardware token;
- something the customer is, such as fingerprint or facial recognition.
Some low-risk transactions may be exempt, but Aurora Bank may still require authentication based on fraud risk, transaction amount, merchant type, new device, new payee, unusual behavior, or regulatory rules.

Aurora Bank will never ask a customer to disclose a full password, full card PIN, or remote-access code.
Additional security checks may delay a payment. Aurora Bank may hold or reject a payment if fraud, sanctions, money laundering, scam, account takeover, or unusual activity indicators are present.

10. Open banking
Open banking allows a customer to give a regulated third-party provider access to account information or payment initiation services. Aurora Bank will provide access only after the customer gives permission through the required secure process.
Important open banking points:
- Aurora Bank will never ask the customer to share online banking passwords with a third-party provider.
- The customer can withdraw open banking consent through Aurora online banking or the third-party provider.
- Revoking access does not delete data already received by the third-party provider.
- The third-party provider is responsible for its own use of data after it receives it.
- Payment initiation through open banking may still require strong customer authentication.
Customers should use only regulated providers and should check the provider name carefully before approving access.

This document explains how Aurora Bank cards work and what customers should do when using cards, ATMs, contactless payments, and mobile wallets. Cards, Debit Cards, Credit Cards, ATMs & Mobile Wallets
8. Card use abroad
Cards may be used abroad where the card scheme and merchant support the transaction. Customers should check travel controls before departure and ensure contact details are up to date.
Foreign currency transactions are converted into the account currency using the card scheme rate, Aurora Bank rate, or a merchant-selected rate, depending on how the transaction is processed. Fees and conversion rules are described in [Fees, Interest & Foreign Exchange](06_fees_interest_and_exchange_rates.md).
A merchant or ATM may offer dynamic currency conversion, allowing payment in the customer’s home currency. This rate is set by the merchant or ATM operator and may be less favorable than Aurora Bank’s standard conversion.

Cards, Debit Cards, Credit Cards, ATMs & Mobile Wallets
1. Card types
Aurora Bank may issue the following card types:
| Card type | Linked to | Main purpose | Key restrictions |
|---|---|---|---|
| Debit card | Current account | Spending the customer’s own available funds | No borrowing unless an overdraft is available. |
| Youth debit card | Youth current account | Controlled spending for customers aged 15 to 17 | Lower limits; no gambling merchants; guardian controls may apply. |
| Credit card | Separate credit-card account | Borrowing up to approved credit limit | Interest, minimum payments, and credit checks apply. |
| Virtual card | Current or credit-card account | Online and mobile wallet payments | May not support ATM cash withdrawal. |
| Replacement card | Existing card account | Replaces lost, stolen, damaged, or expired card | Old card may be cancelled when replacement is issued. |
A card remains property of Aurora Bank and must be returned or destroyed on request.

Cards, Debit Cards, Credit Cards, ATMs & Mobile Wallets
6. Lost, stolen, damaged, or retained card
If a card is lost, stolen, retained by an ATM, or used without permission, the customer should immediately freeze the card in the app and contact Aurora Bank. Emergency contact options are listed in [Glossary, Contact Channels & Service Levels](12_glossary_contact_and_service_level.md).
Aurora Bank may cancel the card and issue a replacement. A replacement-card fee may apply unless the loss was caused by bank error, fraud, expiry, or another fee-waiver circumstance.
Customers should review recent transactions and report unauthorized card transactions promptly under [Disputes, Chargebacks & Fraud Claims](07_disputes_chargebacks_and_fraud_claims.md).

Payments, Transfers & Cutoff Times
This document explains how Aurora Bank processes payments and transfers. It should be read with [Fees, Interest & Foreign Exchange](06_fees_interest_and_exchange_rates.md), [Security, Online Banking & Customer Responsibilities](09_security_online_banking_and_customer_responsibilities.md), and [Disputes, Chargebacks & Fraud Claims](07_disputes_chargebacks_and_fraud_claims.md).

Cards, Debit Cards, Credit Cards, ATMs & Mobile Wallets
7. ATM cash withdrawals and deposits
Customers can use eligible cards at Aurora ATMs and participating network ATMs. ATM operators may charge their own fees or display conversion options. Aurora Bank does not control fees charged by non-Aurora ATM operators.
ATM services may include cash withdrawal, balance inquiry, PIN change, mini-statement, and cash deposit where available. Cash deposits at ATMs may be subject to counting, verification, counterfeit detection, and delayed availability.
Customers should check the ATM area for tampering, shield the PIN, take receipts, and contact Aurora Bank if the ATM does not dispense cash but the account is debited.

| SEPA instant transfer | Usually no once authorized. | Recall can be attempted but is not guaranteed. |
| Standard SEPA transfer | Recall can be requested after execution. | Recipient bank and recipient consent may be required. |
| International wire | Amendment or recall can be requested. | Fees apply and recovery is not guaranteed. |
| Card purchase | Customer should first contact merchant unless fraud is suspected. | Chargeback may be possible under card scheme rules. |

10. Dynamic currency conversion
Dynamic currency conversion occurs when a merchant or ATM offers to charge the customer in the customer’s home currency instead of the local currency. The displayed home-currency amount may include a markup set by the merchant or ATM operator.
Aurora Bank generally recommends that customers compare rates before choosing. Selecting the local currency usually means Aurora Bank or the card scheme performs conversion. Selecting the home currency usually means the merchant or ATM operator performs conversion.
